Bachelor of Business.description:
MIT's Bachelor of Business runs a common first year (business communications, management principles, introductory accounting, marketing principles, information systems fundamentals, economic principles, commercial law and business statistics, several of them CPA-accredited units) before students lock in one of six majors: Accounting, Business Analytics, Contemporary Management, Management, Marketing and Digital Communications, or Professional Accounting. The Accounting and Professional Accounting majors carry CPA-accredited core units, which matters for international students eyeing accounting as a skilled migration occupation. The Business Analytics major overlaps meaningfully with MIT's separate Bachelor of Data Analytics, so applicants choosing between the two should look closely at how technical versus general-business each degree actually is.

As with MIT's other degrees, the pitch is practical and industry-connected teaching in smaller classes than a large public university, a flipped-classroom format, and the InSPIRE academic support scheme built around a cohort that skews heavily international. The degree closes with a mandatory Industry Based Capstone Project in the final trimester.

MIT runs three intakes a year (March, July, November) from both its Melbourne and Sydney campuses.
Bachelor of Business.curriculum:
Common core units: BB101 Business Communications, BB103 Management Principles, BB104 Introductory Accounting (CPA accredited), BB105 Marketing Principles, BN110 Information Systems Fundamentals (CPA accredited), BB106 Economic Principles (CPA accredited), BB107 Commercial Law (CPA accredited), BB108 Business Statistics (CPA accredited), BB313 Critical Thinking and Decision Making, plus the zero credit AIM100 Academic Integrity Module.
Majors (choose one, from Trimester 3): Accounting, Business Analytics, Contemporary Management, Management, Marketing and Digital Communications, Professional Accounting, each with its own major stream units (for example the Management major includes BM202 Organisational Behaviour, BM203 Project Management, BM212 Strategic Human Resource Management, BM302 Strategic Management, BM303 Contemporary Leadership).
Electives: any Bachelor of Business unit from another specialisation stream, subject to prerequisites.
Capstone: BB330 Industry Based Capstone Project (minimum 12 units completed).
Total: 3 years full-time (6 trimesters), 360 credit points, Melbourne or Sydney campus, 3 intakes per year.
Bachelor of Business.admission_requirements: Recent Year 12 completion (VCE, HSC or equivalent, or the International Baccalaureate), meeting relevant state prerequisites (e.g. Victorian Units 3 and 4 study score of at least 20 in English); or full-time equivalent higher education study (assessed if not met); or completion of an AQF Certificate IV or higher from an RTO; or a Foundation Studies/Tertiary Preparatory program; or assessment on work and life experience for applicants who did not complete Year 12. Domestic applicants must be 17 at course commencement; international applicants must be 18.
Bachelor of Business.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78 (component minimums Reading 12, Listening 11, Speaking 17, Writing 20), PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 46), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 162).

Bachelor of Data Analytics.description:
The Bachelor of Data Analytics gives students the data-analytic lifecycle and industry-tool foundations for a career in smart-technology fields such as the Internet of Things, robotics and deep learning, and the growing volumes of data those fields generate. Specialised final-year electives point toward emerging areas including smart technologies and advanced artificial intelligence, alongside deep learning, neural networks and smart-algorithm theory and practice.

Students can pull recommended electives from either MIT's networking unit pool (network security, systems administration, software engineering, cyber security) or its business unit pool (management, accounting, marketing, economics, commercial law, statistics), giving the degree more flexibility than a narrowly technical program. It closes with two mandatory final-year capstone units delivered as an industry-based project.

Runs from both the Melbourne and Sydney campuses across three intakes a year (March, July, November).
Bachelor of Data Analytics.curriculum:
Common core units: BB101 Business Communications, BN112 Computer System Fundamentals, BN106 Networking Fundamentals, BN109 Web and Multimedia Systems, BN110 Information Systems Fundamentals, BN111 Programming Fundamentals, BDA112 Data Science Fundamentals, BDA113 Data Visualisation, BN204 Database Technologies, BDA215 Software Engineering and Project Management, BDA211 Data Warehousing, BDA212 Statistics and Decision Models, BDA213 Data Analytics and Smart Applications, BDA214 Machine Learning, BDA322 Data Science Mathematics, BDA301 Entrepreneurship and Innovation, BDA311 Big Data Applications, BDA312 Deep Learning Applications, plus the zero credit AIM100 Academic Integrity Module.
Recommended electives: Networking stream (BN200 Network Security Fundamentals, BN206 System Administration, BN209 Software Engineering, BN223 Cyber Security Principles, BN231/BN232 Software Development, BN309 Computer Forensics) or Business stream (BB103, BB104, BB105, BB106, BB107, BB108).
Capstone: BDA303 Data Analytics Capstone Project 1, BDA304 Data Analytics Capstone Project 2 (mandatory for the award).
Total: 3 years full-time (6 trimesters), Melbourne or Sydney campus, 3 intakes per year.
Bachelor of Data Analytics.admission_requirements: Recent Year 12 completion (VCE, HSC or equivalent, or the IB), with a Units 3 and 4 study score of at least 20 in both English and Mathematics (or equivalent) as this is an IT program; or full-time equivalent higher education study; or an AQF Certificate IV or higher from an RTO; or a Foundation Studies/Tertiary Preparatory program; or assessment on work and life experience. Domestic applicants must be 17 at course commencement; international applicants must be 18.
Bachelor of Data Analytics.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78 (component minimums Reading 12, Listening 11, Speaking 17, Writing 20), PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 46), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 162).

Bachelor of Engineering Technology (Tele.description:
MIT's Bachelor of Engineering Technology (Telecommunications) is currently in teach-out mode at the Melbourne campus, meaning it is not accepting new commencing students, only continuing existing enrolments through to completion; it remains a real, currently CRICOS-registered and accredited award rather than a discontinued one. The degree covers the planning, design, implementation, management and maintenance of telecommunication systems and networks, with hands-on work on current hardware and software and electives spanning IT, computer networking, systems analysis and security.

The course is designed with input from industry professionals and is aimed at Engineers Australia Stage 1 competency mapping, with a two-part capstone project in the final year that applies theoretical concepts to hands-on design, project management and communication.
Bachelor of Engineering Technology (Tele.curriculum:
Common core units: AIM100 Academic Integrity Module, BE101 Engineering Mathematics, BB101 Business Communications, BE104 Electrical Circuit Fundamentals, BE107 Engineering Mathematics 2, BE102 Digital Systems, BE103 Engineering Practice, BN106 Networking Fundamentals, BE108 Programming for Engineering, BE201 Digital Communication, BN200 Network Security Fundamentals, BE200 Signals and Systems, BN209 Software Engineering, BE700 Industry Experience, BE202 Local and Wide Area Network Technologies, BE203 Telecommunication Systems Engineering, BN205 Project Management, BE204 Embedded Systems, BE301 Telecommunication Modeling and Simulation, BE302 Mobile and Satellite Communication Systems, BN303 Wireless Networks and Security, BE391/BE392 Capstone Project 1 and 2.
Electives: BN223 Cyber Security Principles, BN305 Virtual Private Networks, BN309 Computer Forensics, BN311 IT Security Management, BN323 Ethical Hacking and Security Governance, BN324 Enterprise Cyber Security and Management, BE305 Cloud Engineering, BE393 Software Defined Radio Communications, and several business/networking units.
Total: 3 years full-time (6 trimesters), Melbourne campus only. Currently in teach-out mode, no new intakes.
Bachelor of Engineering Technology (Tele.admission_requirements: Recent Year 12 completion (VCE, HSC or equivalent, or the IB) with the Mathematics and English prerequisites required for IT/engineering programs; or full-time equivalent higher education study; or an AQF Certificate IV or higher from an RTO; or a Foundation Studies/Tertiary Preparatory program; or assessment on work and life experience. Domestic applicants must be 17 at course commencement; international applicants must be 18.
Bachelor of Engineering Technology (Tele.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78, PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 46), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 162), per the course's own English Language Requirements section.

Bachelor of Networking.description:
The Bachelor of Networking builds the practical and theoretical foundations to design, implement, secure and maintain computer network technologies and communication systems, covering hardware, software, programming, information systems, network security, database technologies, software engineering and project management, moving into advanced topics like wireless network security, advanced internetworking design and enterprise cybersecurity.

All Bachelor of Networking degrees share the same 18 core units; students then choose a major in Software Engineering or Cybersecurity, or a Cloud Networks specialisation, and finish with two mandatory final-year industry-based project units. Graduates are prepared for vendor certification paths such as Microsoft Server Administration and Cisco's CCNA family.

Offered from both the Melbourne and Sydney campuses across three intakes a year (March, July, November).
Bachelor of Networking.curriculum:
Common core units (18): AIM100 Academic Integrity Module, BB101 Business Communications, BN110 Information Systems Fundamentals, BN106 Networking Fundamentals, BN108 Programming for Networking, BN109 Web and Multimedia Systems, BN200 Network Security Fundamentals, BN201 Professional Issues of IT, BN202 Internetworking Technologies, BN204 Database Technologies, BN205 Project Management, BN206 System Administration and Management, BN209 Software Engineering, BN321 Advanced Network Design, BN303 Wireless Networks and Security, BN112 Computer System Fundamentals, BN111 Programming Fundamentals, BN317 Cloud Networks.
Major Stream (Cybersecurity or Software Engineering) plus 4 major units (BN223 Cyber Security Principles, BN309 Computer Forensics, BN323 Ethical Hacking and Security Governance, BN324 Enterprise Cybersecurity and Management for the Cybersecurity major).
Electives: Business (BB103, BB104, BB105, BB106, BB107, BB108), Software Engineering (BN314 System Architecture, BN315 Enterprise Architecture).
Capstone: BN301 Industry-Based Project 1, BN304 Industry-Based Project 2 (mandatory).
Total: 3 years full-time (6 trimesters), 360 credit points, Melbourne or Sydney campus, 3 intakes per year.
Bachelor of Networking.admission_requirements: Recent Year 12 completion (VCE, HSC or equivalent, or the IB), with English and Mathematics study-score prerequisites as this is an IT program; or full-time equivalent higher education study; or an AQF Certificate IV or higher from an RTO; or a Foundation Studies/Tertiary Preparatory program; or assessment on work and life experience. Domestic applicants must be 17 at course commencement; international applicants must be 18.
Bachelor of Networking.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78 (component minimums Reading 12, Listening 11, Speaking 17, Writing 20), PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 46), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 162).

Graduate Diploma of Accounting.description:
The Graduate Diploma of Accounting gives graduates from other disciplines a fast, one-year entry point into professional accounting, covering financial and managerial accounting, business statistics, economics, accounting information systems and business and company law. It is positioned as a broad grounding in how accountancy fits into the wider business picture rather than a narrow technical qualification, and provides a pathway into further study such as MIT's own Master of Professional Accounting.

Delivered over 2 trimesters full-time from the Melbourne and Sydney campuses, with three intakes a year.
Graduate Diploma of Accounting.curriculum:
Common core units: GA501 Foundations of Accounting (or MA601 Theory and Current Issues in Accounting for students who qualify), GA508 Business Statistics, GA503 Economics, GA509 Accounting Information Systems, GA511 Financial Accounting and Reporting (prerequisite GA501), GA515 Managerial Accounting (prerequisite GA501), GA514 Business Finance, GA506 Business and Company Law.
Full-time workload is four units (60 credit points) per trimester.
Total: 1 year full-time (2 trimesters), Melbourne or Sydney campus, 3 intakes per year.
Graduate Diploma of Accounting.admission_requirements: An Australian bachelor degree or equivalent in any discipline. Alternative entry available for applicants with at least five years of evidenced managerial work experience.
Graduate Diploma of Accounting.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (no band less than 6.0), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 79 to 93 (component minimums Reading 13, Listening 12, Speaking 18, Writing 21), PTE Academic 59 (no skill below 52), or Cambridge CAE 176 (no band less than 169).

Graduate Diploma of Networking.description:
The Graduate Diploma of Networking covers networking and security topics spanning Internet of Things platforms, sensor networks, LAN/WAN design, VPNs and Cisco networking, aimed at graduates moving into IT and computer networking careers. It runs on a cognate/non-cognate structure: applicants with an IT-related bachelor's degree take a shorter core-plus-elective path (including a Cybersecurity specialisation elective set), while applicants from other disciplines complete two additional foundational units first.

Delivered over 2 trimesters full-time from the Melbourne and Sydney campuses, with three intakes a year.
Graduate Diploma of Networking.curriculum:
Cognate stream common core units: AIM100 Academic Integrity Module, MN511 Enterprise and Cloud Networks, MN522 Information Security, MN504 Networked Application Management, MN521 Network Automation, plus 2 electives (Cybersecurity specialisation electives include MN621 Advanced Network Design, MN506 System Management, MN507 Overview of Software Engineering, MN623 Cybersecurity and Analytics).
Non-cognate stream adds MN404 Fundamentals of Operating Systems and Programming and MN405 Data and Information Management to the same core.
Full-time workload is 60 credit points per trimester (a unit is worth 20 credit points).
Total: 2 trimesters full-time, Melbourne or Sydney campus, 3 intakes per year.
Graduate Diploma of Networking.admission_requirements: Successful completion of an Australian bachelor degree or equivalent. Cognate stream: a bachelor's degree in Information Technology or a related discipline (computer science, software engineering, computer engineering or networking). Non-cognate stream: a bachelor's degree in any other discipline.
Graduate Diploma of Networking.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78 (component minimums Reading 12, Listening 11, Speaking 17, Writing 20), PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 46), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 162).

Master of Artificial Intelligence and Ma.description:
MIT's Master of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning builds from foundational machine learning through neural networks, deep learning, secured AI systems and natural language processing/LLMs to intelligent robotics and vision systems, closing with a dedicated AI Capstone Project. It is one of MIT's newer degrees, developed as demand for applied AI skills has grown, sitting alongside the Master of Data Analytics and Master of Business Analytics as a third, AI-specific postgraduate IT award rather than a duplicate of either.

As with MIT's other postgraduate IT degrees, it runs a cognate/non-cognate entry structure and closes with an industry-based capstone project. Offered from the Sydney and Melbourne campuses across three intakes a year (March, July, November).
Master of Artificial Intelligence and Ma.curriculum:
Common core units: MDA513 ICT Practices, MN404 Fundamentals of Operating Systems and Programming, MAI511 Foundational Machine Learning, MDA522 Artificial Intelligence, MAI521 Neural Networks and Deep Learning, MAI522 Secured AI Systems, MDA611 Predictive Analytics, MDA691 Project Management and Research Methods, MAI611 Natural Language Processing and Large Language Models, MAI621 Intelligent Robotics and Vision Systems, MAI692 AI Capstone Project.
Electives (one, from 500/600-level units): Data Science, Data and Information Management, Mathematical and Statistical Methods, Cyber Security and Analytics, Networked Application Management, IoT and Sensor Networks, Blockchain Technologies and Strategy, Project Management for Entrepreneurs.
Total: 2 years full-time (4 trimesters), 240 credit points, Sydney or Melbourne campus, 3 intakes per year.
Master of Artificial Intelligence and Ma.admission_requirements: Successful completion of an Australian bachelor degree or equivalent. Cognate stream: a bachelor's degree in Information Technology or a related discipline (computer science, software engineering, computer engineering or networking). Non-cognate stream: a bachelor's degree in any other discipline.
Master of Artificial Intelligence and Ma.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78, PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 46), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 162), per the course's own English Language Requirements section.

Master of Business Analytics.description:
The Master of Business Analytics teaches students to analyse data across IT, finance, marketing and business functions and turn it into insight-driven decisions, aimed at students moving from an undergraduate business or IT background into a specialist analytics career. It differs from MIT's Master of Data Analytics in its heavier business-application focus (business intelligence, digital supply chain management, digital marketing analytics) rather than that degree's deeper IT/data-science core, confirming the two are genuinely distinct rather than duplicate offerings.

Students complete a mandatory Research Project for Analytic Professionals followed by a Business Analytics Capstone Project working with a real industry client. Offered from the Sydney and Melbourne campuses across three intakes a year.
Master of Business Analytics.curriculum:
Common core units: AIM100 Academic Integrity Module (mandatory hurdle, 0 credit), MN404 Fundamentals of Operating Systems and Programming, MN405 Data and Information Management, MDA511 Mathematical and Statistical Methods, MBA512 Business Data Analysis, MDA513 ICT Practices, MBA520 Digital Supply Chain Management, MBA522 Business Intelligence, MDA611 Predictive Analytics, MBA691 Research Project for Analytic Professionals, MBA621 Digital Marketing and Analytics, MBA692 Business Analytics Capstone Project.
Electives (one): MDA521 Data Security and Privacy, MDA522 Artificial Intelligence, MDA523 Software Engineering Fundamentals, MDA621 Software Practice for Big Data Analytics, MBA613 Accounting Analytics, MBA628 Business Analytics Applications, MN601 Network Project Management.
Total: 2 years full-time (4 trimesters), Sydney or Melbourne campus, 3 intakes per year.
Master of Business Analytics.admission_requirements: An Australian bachelor degree or equivalent in any discipline.
Master of Business Analytics.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 6.0), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78 (component minimums Reading 13, Listening 12, Speaking 18, Writing 21), PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 52), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 169).

Master of Business Research.description:
The Master of Business Research is a genuine research higher degree, not a coursework master's: after a first-trimester grounding in either a Management stream (management, entrepreneurship and strategic management issues) or an Accounting stream (business analytics, business finance and accounting research issues), students move into dedicated research-skills units and then two full trimesters of supervised Research Thesis, producing an original contribution to the field with potential for journal publication. It functions as both a standalone research credential and a stepping stone toward a PhD.

Offered from the Sydney and Melbourne campuses over 2 years (4 trimesters).
Master of Business Research.curriculum:
Core research units: MR501 Research Skills, MR502 Quantitative and Qualitative Research Techniques, MR601 Research Proposal and Literature Review, MR603 Research Thesis 1 (prerequisite MR601), MR604 Research Thesis 2 (prerequisite MR603).
Stream elective units: Management stream (MBR505 Management Issues, MBR525 Entrepreneurship Issues, MBR516 Strategic Management Issues for Research Projects) or Accounting stream (MBR509 Business Analytics and Data Intelligence Issues, MBR511 Auditing Issues, MBR514 Business Finance Issues, MBR517 Forensic Accounting Issues), plus focused electives (MBR519 Accounting Research Approaches, MBR512 Accounting Research Ethics for the Accounting stream; MBR516 for Management).
Structure: one trimester of stream units, one trimester of research-skills units, two trimesters of supervised Research Thesis.
Total: 2 years full-time (4 trimesters), Sydney or Melbourne campus, research higher degree (no elective specialisation beyond Management/Accounting streams).
Master of Business Research.admission_requirements: A bachelor's or master's degree in any field of study from an Australian higher education institution, or a qualification recognised as equivalent to an Australian bachelor's degree by the National Office of Overseas Skills Recognition (NOOSR). Applicants from a non-cognate background are reviewed individually and may be assigned conditional foundation studies before admission.
Master of Business Research.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (no band less than 6.0), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 79 to 93 (component minimums Reading 13, Listening 12, Speaking 18, Writing 21), PTE Academic 59 (no skill below 52), or Cambridge CAE 176 (no band less than 169).

Master of Data Analytics (MDA).description:
The Master of Data Analytics (MDA) trains students to combine statistics and data with technology to analyse large structured and unstructured datasets, running a cognate/non-cognate entry structure (an IT-background cognate stream and a broader non-cognate stream that first covers foundational IT units). Students can specialise via an IoT Data Analytics or Cloud Networks elective stream, and the degree is accredited by the Australian Computer Society (ACS) at the Professional Level.

It is a genuinely distinct degree from both the undergraduate Bachelor of Data Analytics and the Master of Business Analytics: MDA's core is IT/data-science-heavy (data science, data security, predictive analytics, big-data software practice) rather than the business-application focus of the Business Analytics master's. The final-year Data Analytics Capstone Project is an industry-based unit. Offered from the Sydney and Melbourne campuses across three intakes a year.
Master of Data Analytics (MDA).curriculum:
Cognate stream common core units: AIM100 Academic Integrity Module, MDA511 Mathematical and Statistical Methods, MDA512 Data Science, MDA513 ICT Practices, MDA521 Data Security and Privacy, MDA522 Artificial Intelligence, MDA611 Predictive Analytics, MDA691 Project Management and Research Methods, MDA621 Software Practice for Big Data Analytics, MDA692 Data Analytics Capstone Project.
Non-cognate stream adds MN404 Fundamentals of Operating Systems and Programming and MN405 Data and Information Management, with students who have gaps in undergraduate studies also required to complete these.
Elective specialisations (3 electives, one stream): IoT Data Analytics or Cloud Networks.
Total: 2 years full-time (4 trimesters), 240 credit points (12 units of 20 credit points), Sydney or Melbourne campus, 3 intakes per year.
Master of Data Analytics (MDA).admission_requirements: Successful completion of an Australian bachelor degree or equivalent. Cognate stream: a bachelor's degree in Information Technology or a related discipline (computer science, software engineering, computer engineering or networking). Non-cognate stream: a bachelor's degree in any other discipline.
Master of Data Analytics (MDA).english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 6.0), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78 (component minimums Reading 13, Listening 12, Speaking 18, Writing 21), PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 52), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 169).

Master of Engineering (Telecommunication.description:
MIT's Master of Engineering (Telecommunications) is currently in teach-out mode at the Melbourne campus, meaning it is not accepting new commencing students, only continuing existing enrolments through to completion; it remains a real, currently CRICOS-registered and accredited award rather than a discontinued one. The course covers advanced networking, antennas in mobile and satellite communication systems, digital signal processing and telecommunication modelling and simulation, and is designed to meet Engineers Australia accreditation requirements.

A mandatory ME700 Industry Experience placement (12 weeks full-time or 24 weeks part-time) plus two capstone project units give graduates real workplace exposure supervised jointly by academic staff and an industry partner.
Master of Engineering (Telecommunication.curriculum:
Common core units: AIM100 Academic Integrity Module, ME504 Advanced Networking, ME505 Antennas in Mobile and Satellite Communication Systems, ME502 Overview of Digital Communication, ME606 Digital Signal Processing, ME600 Engineering Project Management, ME503 Telecommunication System Engineering, ME700 Industry Experience, ME603 Project 1, ME601 Telecommunication Modelling and Simulation, ME604 Project 2, ME602 Mobile and Personal Communication Systems.
Electives (two): ME501 Professional Engineering Practice, ME605 Cloud Engineering, ME693 Software-Defined Radio Communication, MN504 Networked Application Management, MN506 System Management, MN507 Overview of Software Engineering.
Total: 2 years full-time (4 trimesters), Melbourne campus only. Currently in teach-out mode, no new intakes.
Master of Engineering (Telecommunication.admission_requirements: An Australian bachelor degree, or equivalent, of at least four years duration in an area of Engineering related to Telecommunications, Electronics, or Electrical Engineering.
Master of Engineering (Telecommunication.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78, PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 46), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 162), per the course's own English Language Requirements section.

Master of ICT Research.description:
The Master of ICT Research is a genuine research higher degree spanning three specialised streams (Networking, Data Analytics and Telecommunications), combining an initial semester of elective coursework units with a formal Research Proposal and Methodologies unit and then two semesters of supervised Research Thesis. Research areas span cloud computing, cybersecurity, machine learning, AI, data science, software engineering, telecommunications engineering, computational intelligence, micro robotics, mechatronics and remote sensing.

Graduates are positioned for research-oriented professional roles in higher education or industry; MIT's own materials cite an average entry-level salary range of AUD 70,000 to 100,000 for non-doctorate researcher roles in Australia. Offered from the Sydney and Melbourne campuses over 2 years (4 semesters), with MN404 and MN405 available for students whose undergraduate background has gaps in foundational ICT knowledge.
Master of ICT Research.curriculum:
Core units: MR901 Applied Research, MR902 Research Proposal and Methodologies, MR603 Research Thesis 1 (prerequisite: successful completion of all first-year units), MR604 Research Thesis 2 (prerequisite MR603).
Elective units: MAI521 Neural Networks and Deep Learning, MAI522 Secured AI Systems, MDA512 Data Science, MDA521 Data Security and Privacy, MDA522 Artificial Intelligence, MDA523 Software Engineering Fundamentals, MN521 Network Automation, MN522 Information Security, MN603 Wireless Networks and Security, MN623 Cyber Security and Analytics.
Advanced electives (at least one required): MAI611 Natural Language Processing and Large Language Models, MAI621 Intelligent Robotics and Vision Systems, MDA611 Predictive Analytics, MDA621 Software Practice for Big Data Analytics, MN624 Digital Forensics, MN625 Software Managed Networks.
Structure: one semester of elective/applied-research units, one semester of the Research Proposal and Methodologies unit, two semesters of supervised Research Thesis.
Total: 2 years full-time (4 semesters), Sydney or Melbourne campus, research higher degree.
Master of ICT Research.admission_requirements: A completed Australian bachelor degree or equivalent in any ICT discipline. Other qualifications and experience may, upon application, be deemed equivalent to the coursework units by the Institute's Academic Board.
Master of ICT Research.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (no band less than 6.0), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 79 to 93 (component minimums Reading 13, Listening 12, Speaking 18, Writing 21), PTE Academic 59 (no skill below 52), or Cambridge CAE 176 (no band less than 169).

Master of Networking.description:
The Master of Networking gives students ten core units in networking, security and IT fundamentals, then a choice of specialisation major (Cybersecurity, Cloud Networks, Smart Sensors and Automation, Cryptocurrency, or Project Management) via two additional elective units, or the option to complete the degree without a major for a broader networking/IT skillset. The degree runs a cognate/non-cognate entry structure, with non-cognate applicants (a bachelor's in any discipline other than IT) admitted on the same core but expected to build foundational IT knowledge through the shared MN404/MN405 units.

Final-year students complete a mandatory MN690 Research Methods and Project Management unit followed by an MN692 Capstone Project. Offered from the Sydney and Melbourne campuses across three intakes a year (March, July, November).
Master of Networking.curriculum:
Common core units: MN404 Fundamentals of Operating Systems and Programming, MN405 Data and Information Management, MN511 Enterprise and Cloud Networks, MN521 Network Automation, MN522 Information Security, MDA513 ICT Practices, MN603 Wireless Networks and Security, MN625 Software Managed Networks, MN690 Research Methods and Project Management, MN692 Capstone Project.
Specialisation electives (2, one specialisation): Cybersecurity (MN623 Cyber Security and Analytics, MN624 Digital Forensics), Cloud Networks (MN504 Networked Application Management, MN506 System Management), Smart Sensors and Automation (MDA541 IoT and Sensor Networks, MDA641 Smart Environments), Cryptocurrency (MN631 Blockchain Technologies and Strategy, MDA632 Cryptofinance and Legal Framework), Project Management (MN641 Project Management for Entrepreneurs, MN642 Project Governance and Resource Management).
Total: 2 years full-time (4 trimesters), Sydney or Melbourne campus, 3 intakes per year.
Master of Networking.admission_requirements: Successful completion of an Australian bachelor degree or equivalent. Cognate stream: a bachelor's degree in Information Technology or a related discipline (computer science, software engineering, computer engineering or networking). Non-cognate stream: a bachelor's degree in any other discipline.
Master of Networking.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.0 (no band less than 5.5), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 60 to 78 (component minimums Reading 12, Listening 11, Speaking 17, Writing 20), PTE Academic 52 (no skill below 46), or Cambridge CAE 169 (no band less than 162).

Master of Professional Accounting.description:
The Master of Professional Accounting gives graduates from any discipline a broad grounding in accounting and how it fits into the wider business picture, covering foundations of accounting, economics, business statistics, accounting information systems, business and company law, financial and managerial accounting, auditing, taxation law and accounting research, closing with a mandatory Industry Based Capstone Project. It is designed as a professional-accreditation-oriented pathway (CPA Australia/CAANZ-relevant units) for career changers rather than a research degree.

Offered from the Sydney and Melbourne campuses over 2 years (4 trimesters), with three intakes a year.
Master of Professional Accounting.curriculum:
Common core units: AIM100 Academic Integrity Module, MA501 Foundations of Accounting, MA503 Economics, MA508 Business Statistics, MA509 Accounting Information Systems, MA506 Business and Company Law, MA511 Financial Accounting and Reporting (prerequisite MA501), MA514 Business Finance (prerequisite MA508), MA515 Managerial Accounting (prerequisite MA501), MA601 Theory and Current Issues in Accounting (prerequisite MA511), MA611 Auditing (prerequisite MA506 and MA511), MA613 Taxation Law (prerequisite MA506), MA609 Business Analytics and Data Intelligence (prerequisite MA508), MA618 Industry Based Capstone Project (prerequisite: minimum 10 units completed), MA619 Accounting Research (prerequisite MA601 and MA515), plus 2 elective units.
Total: 2 years full-time (4 trimesters), 240 credit points, Sydney or Melbourne campus, 3 intakes per year.
Master of Professional Accounting.admission_requirements: An Australian bachelor degree or equivalent qualification in any discipline.
Master of Professional Accounting.english_requirements: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (no band less than 6.0), or equivalent TOEFL iBT 79 to 93 (component minimums Reading 13, Listening 12, Speaking 18, Writing 21), PTE Academic 59 (no skill below 52), or Cambridge CAE 176 (no band less than 169).
